To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
audience segmentation using psychosocial and demographic factors outperformed audience segmentation based on demographic factors alone.

psychosocial factors are the most important predictors of physical activity in this sample, and that audience segmentation based on a combination of psychosocial and demographic factors yields the greatest improvement over no segmentation.

audience segmentation based on a combination of demographic, health status, and psychosocial variables is more effective at creating more homogeneous subgroups than segmentation based on any single variable type alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing a new approach to audience segmentation for physical-activity promotion.
the development of an audience segmentation strategy to target physical activity promotion interventions to the most appropriate population subgroups.

the development of a theory-based segmentation approach that can identify subgroups of people that are homogeneous with regard to certain variables that are associated with physical activity and can be targeted for specific intervention strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most homogeneous groups are formed by using a combination of psychosocial and demographic variables, and these groups are better than any of the individual types of variables.

the best segmentation is achieved by combining all variables, but the best segmentation for a specific intervention is dependent on the specific variables that have been found to be associated with that intervention.

audience segmentation based on psychosocial variables and health status factors in conjunction with demographic characteristics provides the greatest number of segments with the greatest variability in physical activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
audience segmentation is a promising approach to developing more effective and efficient physical activity promotion programs.

psychosocial and demographic variables are more useful than health status variables in identifying subgroups that differ in their physical activity levels and that the combination of all three variables provides the most useful audience segmentation.

audience segmentation based on psychosocial and demographic variables provides the most homogeneous subgroups, but the most important variables to include in audience segmentation are the psychosocial ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
audience segmentation can be a useful tool for developing targeted interventions to promote physical activity.

the use of audience segmentation strategies that rely on a combination of demographic, health status, and psychosocial variables can improve the identification of homogeneous subgroups that can be targeted by physical activity promotion interventions.
audience segmentation is most useful when it is based on psychosocial factors.
